title: Monorepo, pnpm Workspaces & Repository Foundation
outcome: Create a pnpm monorepo whose boundaries, scripts, shared configuration, and dependency ownership are understandable before feature code grows.
artifact: TaskFlow repository root with apps/web, apps/api, shared packages, workspace metadata, root scripts, and clean Git hygiene.
labSteps: Create the repository root and initialize Git before generating applications.
Declare workspace globs and explain why apps and packages are separate categories.
Create web and API workspaces without copying node_modules between them.
Create a shared TypeScript configuration package and consume it through workspace dependencies.
Add root dev/build/typecheck/test scripts that delegate to workspaces.
Inspect pnpm why/list output so you can explain where a dependency is owned and why.
failureModes: Installing app-only dependencies at workspace root
Duplicating tsconfig settings in every package
Using relative imports across app boundaries instead of package contracts
Committing build output, environment files, or node_modules
mastery: Can run one app and the whole repository intentionally
Can add a shared package without circular dependencies
principles: A monorepo should make shared ownership and coordinated changes easier, not merely put folders in one repository.
Use pnpm workspaces to make package boundaries explicit and dependency installation deterministic.
Keep shared configuration in dedicated packages instead of duplicating compiler and lint settings.
Run repository-wide tasks from the root while allowing app-specific commands when debugging.
